elements.element: Customer (Licensee) has a right to terminate for convenience
elements.evidence: "Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience"

elements.element: Notice period of 30 days, in writing
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor"

elements.element: Pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on such termination
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination"

elements.element: Vendor (Licensor) has no termination-for-convenience right during the committed term
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Initial Period or any extension thereof"
"thirty (30) days' prior written notice" — shorter than the 60–90 day fallback band

elements.element: Early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "no early termination fee or other penalty shall be payable by Licensee" (zero is within the cap)

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at end of a term on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: insertion bars Licensor convenience termination entirely; no 90-day end-of-term mechanic

offending_extra_words: and no early termination fee or other penalty shall be payable by Licensee
reasons: All four atomic elements of the preferred position are expressly delivered by the new paragraph IV: Licensee convenience right, 30 days' written notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and an express bar on Licensor convenience termination during the Initial Period or extensions.

The fallback is not satisfied on its own terms (notice is 30 rather than 60–90 days and Licensor is given no end-of-term convenience right), but that is irrelevant because the locked target is preferred and the preferred bargain is fully met; the levels are not mixed.

Minimality is slightly exceeded: "in whole or in part" imports a partial-termination scope the playbook position does not require, and the added "no early termination fee or other penalty" is duplicative protection on top of the pro-rata refund entitlement (the preferred position simply omits any exit fee rather than negating one).

Intent is preserved: the original term, renewal, breach-termination and extension mechanics are untouched, the insertion uses the existing defined term "Initial Period", and no contradiction or dangling mechanic is created.

Note: the deterministic "Customer convenience termination present" check reports false, but the operative inserted text plainly grants Licensee a convenience right on 30 days' notice; the failed automated check appears to be a detection artefact rather than a substantive gap.
